text: Don't fight those in power if you have no chance to win.
Don't argue with those who have plenty of gold— they will drag you down by bribing others or by persuading the king to see things their way.
And arguing with those who talk too much is like piling more wood on a fire.
Don't laugh at those who are crude, unless you want to hear them insult your ancestors.
If people are trying to stop committing sins, don't make them feel guilty; remember that we all deserve to be punished for our sins.
Don't dishonor old people— the rest of us are getting older too.
Never be happy when someone dies. Remember, all of us must die someday.
When wise people speak, pay attention, then study what they have said. You will learn discipline and how to serve those in power.
Listen when old people tell you what they learned from their ancestors. Then you will understand how to give the best answer when one is needed.
Don't encourage sinners to sin; they might blaze up like a fire and you would get burned.
Don't argue with the arrogant— they will try to turn your own words against you.
Never lend to someone who is stronger than you; if you make such a loan, don't count on being repaid.
Don't ever guarantee a loan for more than you can afford, and don't be surprised if you have to repay a loan you guaranteed.
Never sue judges— their influence is so great that they will always win.
Don't travel with those who like danger. They will do what they please and cause you problems, and their foolishness might get you killed.
Don't start a fight with hot-tempered people. They don't care who they kill, so don't travel with them along deserted roads, where you would be helpless if they attacked.
Fools can't keep a secret, so don't ask them for advice.
And when strangers are around don't do anything that you want kept secret— you never know who they might tell.
Do not discuss with just anyone what you really think, and don't let others do favors for you.
